note_add: Campers owe no separate entrance fee: residents who paid the state parks fee with their vehicle registration enter free, and the non-resident camping fee already includes the non-resident's daily entrance fee. A non-resident holding the Nonresident Entrance Pass pays the resident camping fee instead. The non-resident premium is $10 a night at standard and electric sites and $8 at rustic sites. The state accommodations tax is included in the posted camping fee. A site takes up to eight people, with no per-person fee. The schedule has no weekend or holiday rate. It does have a peak season (third Friday in May to third Sunday in September) and an off-season rate, and premium campsites cost $5 more in peak season. The schedule's daily entrance authorizes one non-resident vehicle, so a second non-resident vehicle may owe its own entrance fee. No camping fee for an extra vehicle is published. Sluice Boxes and Medicine Rocks charge Montana residents no camping fee.

note_add: Every vehicle entering a park needs a daily vehicle pass or an annual pass. The pass is separate from the camping fee. From May 1, 2026 the out-of-state plate rate is $15; State Forest, Chatfield, Golden Gate Canyon, Elkhead, Pearl Lake, Stagecoach and Steamboat Lake charge $2 more. A daily pass is valid through noon the next day, so one night needs one pass. A car towed or carried by a motorhome gets a free pass with a camping permit or reservation; slide-in truck campers do not qualify. Coloradans can buy the $29 Keep Colorado Wild pass with their vehicle registration. One camping unit and up to six people per site. Regulations allow one vehicle besides the camping equipment, and many parks allow a second if space allows (it needs its own pass). Campground permits are not split by residency; the non-resident difference is only in the vehicle pass. Posted camping fees do not include accommodations tax.

note_add: A camping permit covers day use of the park through 9 p.m. on the day it expires, so campers buy no separate day-use permit. Day use alone is $5 a vehicle for residents and $10 for non-residents; residents are exempt October 1 through April 30. Camping is charged per vehicle per night: each vehicle in the park overnight pays its own camping fee, and a motorhome with its towed car counts as one vehicle. The non-resident premium is $5 on primitive and developed sites; under the rule, hookup fees (water $5, electric $10, sewer $5) are the same for everyone. The division's camping page gives combined hookup prices that differ by $5-10. There is no per-person charge. The ReserveAmerica fee is $3.50 a night, at most $10 a reservation.
